Deputies passed a new text for the Integrity Bill, after the Constitutional Court ruled that an article regarding the declaration of public officials’ wealth was inconsistent with the Constitution. Save Romania Union proposed that the National Integrity Agency release a file on each public official, disclosing the interests relevant to their position within 60 days of their submission of wealth and interest declarations. It was also agreed that such files should be filled in as of January 1, 2027. The bill with the accepted amendments now goes to the Senate for a final decision. Senators are fast-tracking debates on the Hydrogen Law, a key milestone without which the country risks losing a EUR 2.84 billion payment. The endorsement of the new public sector salary law, a crucial PNRR milestone tied to EUR 770 million, remains uncertain. Despite the August 31 deadline, the bill remains under party review. DRONE A military drone that entered Romanian airspace on Monday morning and was most likely also caught on camera above the town of Tecuci, in Galaţi County, crashed the same afternoon in a household in Vrancea County. No casualties were reported. Residents about 300 meters around the impact area were evacuated as a precaution, and the area was isolated. After completing the checks, the defence ministry reported the aircraft did not carry explosives. According to the institution, at around 6:00 AM, the radar surveillance system detected intermittent signals in the airspace of the Republic of Moldova, near Cahul. One of them later appeared in Galaţi County, and a RO-ALERT message was sent to the public. Two Romanian Air Force F-16 aircraft and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter were sent to monitor the situation. UKRAINE The “Coalition of the Willing”, made up of over 30 countries supporting Ukraine, convened in Kyiv on Monday to discuss new ways of support. The meeting was also attended by Romania’s president Nicușor Dan via a conference call. He congratulated Ukraine on its 35th independence anniversary and highlighted the courage and resilience of the Ukrainian nation in the face of war. “Romania will continue to stand by Ukraine, steadfast in supporting the independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity of this country. Ukraine can count on our multidimensional help,” the Romanian leader posted on the social media platform X. The head of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, announced the European Union is releasing a new instalment of over EUR 6 billion for Ukraine, which will enable it to strengthen its air defence and procure missiles and ammunition. The French president Emmanuel Macron has pledged to speed up deliveries of anti-aircraft missiles to counter Russian attacks, and has called on other partners to follow suit. The support is crucial for Ukraine, whose cities and infrastructure are under daily attack by Moscow’s military. AMBASSADOR The Ambassador of Ukraine to Bucharest, Ihor Prokopchuk, stated on the occasion of Ukraine’s Independence Day on Monday that Romania is a key partner for his country in areas such as security, energy, transport and infrastructure, regional development and European integration. We greatly appreciate Romania’s constant support for Ukraine’s European path, the diplomat said in a video message. I take this opportunity to express my special gratitude to the Romanian state and the Romanian people in all social categories for their solidarity with Ukraine, for the support provided to Ukrainians who have found shelter in Romania, as well as for their assistance, Ihor Prokopciuk also said. CURRENCY Uncertainties stemming from the domestic political situation pose a direct risk to the exchange rate of the Leu, the National Bank of Romania (BNR) warned in the minutes of its latest monetary policy meeting. The Bank highlighted additional elevated risks tied to the escalating conflict in the Middle East and, above all, the country’s twin fiscal and trade deficits. The central bank stressed the critical need for political and governmental stability, alongside a continued fiscal correction to bring both deficits under control. WILDFIRES Romanian firefighters deployed to Serbia remain active on the ground, intervening across multiple sectors affected by severe wildfires at the request of Serbian authorities, according to the General Inspectorate for Emergencies (IGSU). Operating through the day and overnight with specialised fire trucks and equipment, the teams are focusing on containing the blazes and preventing their spread toward nearby residential communities. IGSU reaffirmed that Romanian emergency personnel continue to work alongside their Serbian counterparts to manage the crisis and limit environmental damage. Abundantia, exhibition view “Still-life / Still Alive” (2026) © Schirn Kunsthalle Frankfurt 2026, photo: Moritz Bernoully. FRANKFURT .- Anna Hulačová’s figurative sculptures combine influences from Surrealism, Socialist Realism, and Czech folk art to create a distinctive cosmos of their own. From October 1, 2026, to January 10, 2027, the Schirn Kunsthalle Frankfurt is presenting the artist’s first solo exhibition in Germany, coinciding with the Czech Republic’s appearance as Guest of Honour at the Frankfurt Book Fair 2026. Hulačová, who grew up on a farm, draws on a deep connection to plants and animals in her artistic practice, exploring the relationship between humans, nature, and technology from an ecofeminist perspective. Her work addresses the loss of biodiversity, declining insect populations, and the consequences of industrial agriculture. The bee—a symbol of collective labor, ecological crisis, and mystical immortality—is a central metaphor in her work, but its role extends beyond the symbolic: Hulačová creates her works in collaboration with her own bee colonies. Together, the artist and the bees produce hybrid creatures and faceless science-fiction figures in which concrete and honeycomb, the organic and the technological, nature and machine merge. The exhibition at the Schirn presents sculptures, reliefs, and installations, many of which were created specifically for the occasion. The exhibition’s title refers to the figure of Abundantia, the Roman personification of prosperity and abundance. Her attribute, the cornucopia, magically pours forth its riches, while the resources, effort, and labor on which prosperity depends remain invisible. The exhibition “Anna Hulačová: Abundantia” is supported by the Ministry of Culture of the Czech Republic and the Moravian Library as part of the country’s Guest of Honour appearance at the Frankfurt Book Fair 2026, with additional support from the German-Czech Future Fund as well as the foundations Dr. Hans Feith und Dr. Elisabeth Feith-Stiftung and Kummer-Vanotti-Stiftung. The education and outreach program is supported by the Polytechnische Gesellschaft Foundation, Frankfurt am Main. SEBASTIAN BADEN, DIRECTOR OF THE SCHIRN: “Anna Hulačová is one of the most compelling artists of the younger generation in the Czech Republic. Her engagement with the legacy of socialist visual traditions and the cultural landscape they shaped has given rise to an important perspective. With her distinctive artistic language, Hulačová demonstrates a keen awareness of pressing issues, such as the industrialization of agriculture, the consequences of monoculture, and the loss of biodiversity.” MARTINA WEINHART, CURATOR OF THE EXHIBITION: “Anna Hulačová addresses our alienated relationship with nature. Trained as a wood sculptor, she creates her work through an unusual process of co-creation with her bee colonies, which swarm into the cavities of her sculptures and fill them with honeycomb. Hulačová brings these elements together in science-fiction tableaux of an ecofeminist future that combine utopia and dystopia, antiquity and the present, myth and a radical engagement with the here and now.” For her solo exhibition at the Schirn, Anna Hulačová has created two distinct installations. The first gallery features imposing machine-like sculptures in concrete, such as Engine (2026) and Big Machine (2026). Concrete reliefs suspended from the ceiling feature delicate graphite drawings and are combined with carved linden wood or honeycomb. Here, Hulačová references the reliefs commonly found on socialist-era buildings, drawing on familiar motifs and forms from this visual tradition, such as upward-reaching stalks of grain. At the Schirn, she combines these elements with the sculptures Alien Bees (2021 and 2026) to surreal effect. The insect-like figures have humanoid features and recall comics and science-fiction films from the 1950s. The second gallery features the newly produced installation Still Life / Still Alive (2026), a food conveyor belt flanked by metallic, clinical-looking walls. Figures of female workers are positioned throughout the space. At the end of the conveyor belt, fruit has accumulated in a large pile, while one worker attempts to tackle the abundance of produce with a whisk. The work also references conventions of representation in Western (male-dominated) art history, in which women were frequently associated with an abundance of fruit, as in sixteenth-century depictions of market scenes. At the same time, it points to the exploitation of (female) labor in food production, both historically and today, as well as to women’s role as consumers at the end of a long, highly specialized and mechanized chain of production. The second work in the gallery, After Bugonia (2025), addresses the dairy industry. Three female workers in rubber boots, work coats, and headscarves recall the figures of Socialist Realism in both bearing and aesthetic. This totalitarian art promoted the archetype of the mother through concepts such as land, earth, and fertility. The workers’ heads are either faceless or filled with honeycomb. The title After Bugonia derives from an ancient myth according to which colonies of bees were spontaneously generated from the carcass of a bull. The motif of the bee thus brings together multiple layers of meaning. As a female collective, bees—evoked in expressions such as “busy as a bee”—also become a symbol of the oft invisible labor of women across different societies. ANNA HULAČOVÁ (b. 1984 in Sušice, Czechoslovakia, now Czech Republic) graduated from the Academy of Fine Arts in Prague, where she studied in the Studio of Intermedia Work II under Jiří Příhoda. She has exhibited her work at various institutions and exhibitions, including CEAAC in Strasbourg, the National Gallery Prague, Galeria Arsenał in Białystok, House of Arts Brno, Art Encounters Biennial 2021 in Timișoara, MO.CO. Montpellier, the Centre Pompidou and Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris, the Regional Gallery in Liberec, the East Slovak Gallery in Košice, the 2019 Aichi Triennale in Japan, Casino Luxembourg, Baltic Triennial 13, Prague City Gallery, Gdańsk City Gallery, and the 22nd Bienal de Arte Contemporânea Sesc_Videobrasil in São Paulo. https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/10/31/ujab.text: Menü Kereső Újabb jelöltet neveztek ENSZ-főtitkárnak, nem Orbán Viktor az Külföld frissítve Ignácz Péter Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Törökország hivatalosan is jelölte Feridun Sinirlioğlu-t, az Európai Biztonsági és Együttműködési Szervezet (EBESZ) főtitkárát az ENSZ főtitkári posztjára – közölte szombaton az Anadolu török állami hírügynökség, külügyminisztériumi forrásokra hivatkozva. Az erről szóló levelet pénteken adta át a török ENSZ-nagykövet a Biztonsági Tanács és a Közgyűlés vezetőinek – írta a hírügynökség. A Recep Tayyip Erdoğan török elnök által írt levélben az államfő Sinirlioğlu 40 éves diplomáciai tapasztalatát említette, ami alatt külügyminiszterként és ENSZ-nagykövetként is szolgált, és akinek nagy tudása van az ENSZ működéséről. Ankara a jelölést az Anadolu forrásai szerint azután nyújtotta be, hogy Biztonsági Tanácsban a jelenlegi jelöltek támogatottságát mérő legutóbbi, péntek próbaszavazás nem hozott egyértelmű eredményt. Ezzel nyolcra emelkedett a jelenleg versenyben lévő jelöltek száma. A jelöltek közül a 15 tagú Biztonsági Tanács választja ki, hogy kit nevez a posztra, és ezután a Közgyűlés dönt. A BT-ben kilenc szavazat kell ahhoz, hogy valakit hivatalosan főtitkárnak jelöljenek, de az öt állandó tagnak, az Egyesült Államoknak, Kínának, Oroszországnak, Nagy-Britanniának és Franciaországnak vétójoga van. A BT-ben próbaszavazásokat szoktak tartani a jelöltekről, és azokon általában szeptemberre már ki szokott alakulni, hogy ki az egy-két leginkább esélyes jelölt, de idén egyikük sem került egyértelműen az élre. A pénteki, hetedik szavazáson Rebeca Grynspan Mayufis, Costa Rica volt alelnöke, az ENSZ Kereskedelmi és Fejlesztési Konferenciájának (UNCTAD) főtitkára kapta a legtöbb bátorító szavazatot, 11-et, de négyen ellenezték jelölését. A második helyen Rafael Grossi, a Nemzetközi Atomenergia-ügynökség (NAÜ) főigazgatója, volt argentin diplomata végzett, kilenc bátorító és négy ellenkező szavazattal, kettő tartózkodás mellett. Azt azonban nem lehet tudni, hogy az ellenkezők között vannak-e a BT vétójoggal rendelkező állandó tagjai. A hatodik szavazáson ezt jelezték, és akkor Grynspan és Grossi jelölését is két állandó tag ellenezte. Hivatalosan még senki sem jelölte Orbán Viktort, akinek nevét egy hete kezdték el emlegetni lehetséges ENSZ-főtitkárként. Nevének bedobása nagy port vert fel, és pont ez lehetett a cél. Erről ebben a cikkünkben írtunk részletesen . A héten Jean-Noël Barrot francia külügyminiszter jelezte , hogy Párizs ellezi Orbán Viktor jelölését. Egy szenátor kérdésére válaszolva közölte, hogy "az ENSZ-főtitkári tisztség nem szolgálhat vigaszdíjként egy olyan vezető számára, akit a választásokon legyőztek, akit saját népe távolított el a hatalomból. Egyben közölte, hogy nem fogadják el, hogy alapjaiban meggyengítsék vagy megbénítsák olyan nagyhatalmak, amelyek szabad kezet szeretnének maguknak.
